context: You are training to be a guide at the university's science museum. Listen to your supervisor and repeat what she says.
visual: A bright museum hall with a dinosaur skeleton in the centre and a family looking at a fossil display.
sentences: Welcome to the science museum.
Please stay with your group.
This skeleton is about seventy million years old.
Visitors may touch the fossils on the blue table.
The planetarium show begins every hour on the second floor.
If anyone feels lost, they should look for a staff member wearing a green badge.
Before the tour ends, remind everyone that the gift shop closes thirty minutes before the museum does.

context: You are a new assistant at the campus library help desk. Listen to the head librarian and repeat what he says.
visual: A library help desk with a computer, a stack of returned books and a sign that says Information.
sentences: Good morning, how can I help?
Books are due in three weeks.
You can renew your loans on the library website.
Group study rooms must be booked at least a day ahead.
Students who return books late will receive an email reminder first.
The quiet reading area on the top floor is reserved for silent individual study.
If a student cannot find a book on the shelf, check the catalogue to see whether it has been borrowed.

context: You are working as a lab assistant in the chemistry department. Listen to the lab manager and repeat what she says.
visual: A chemistry lab with students in white coats and safety glasses standing at long benches.
sentences: Put on your safety glasses.
Never eat or drink in the lab.
Each bench has its own sink and fire blanket.
Chemicals must be returned to the locked cabinet after use.
Please label every container clearly with the date and your initials.
If something spills, tell the instructor immediately instead of trying to clean it up yourself.
At the end of each session, students should wipe down their benches and switch off all the gas valves.

context: You have a summer job at a city botanical garden. Listen to the head gardener and repeat what he says.
visual: A large glass greenhouse full of tropical plants, with a wooden path running through it.
sentences: This is the tropical greenhouse.
The air here is very humid.
Most of these plants come from South America.
Visitors should stay on the wooden path at all times.
We water the orchids early in the morning before the doors open.
Some of the plants in this room can only survive at temperatures above twenty degrees.
When guests ask about buying seeds, send them to the visitor centre beside the main entrance on the east side.

context: You are volunteering at the orientation week information tent. Listen to the student coordinator and repeat what she says.
visual: A white tent on a campus lawn with maps, free water bottles and a banner reading Orientation Week.
sentences: Hi, welcome to campus!
Here is a map of the university.
The student center is right across the main square.
New students can pick up their ID cards at the registrar's office.
There is a free campus tour leaving from this tent every forty-five minutes.
International students should attend the visa information session on Wednesday afternoon in the main auditorium.
If someone asks about housing problems, give them the residence office phone number printed on the back of the map.

context: You are training as a guide at an art gallery. Listen to the senior guide and repeat what he says.
visual: A gallery room with large landscape paintings on white walls and a small group of visitors listening to a guide.
sentences: Please follow me this way.
Photography without flash is allowed.
This room contains paintings from the nineteenth century.
The artist painted most of these landscapes near the coast.
Notice how the light changes from one side of the canvas to the other.
Many critics at the time disliked this style, but it later became extremely popular.
Before we move on, I'd like you to compare this painting with the smaller one hanging beside the window.

context: You are starting work as a research assistant in a psychology lab. Listen to the principal investigator and repeat what she says.
visual: A small room with a computer, a desk, two chairs and a consent form lying next to a pair of headphones.
sentences: Greet each participant warmly.
Ask them to read the consent form.
Participants can leave the study at any time without penalty.
Keep all of their personal information in the locked filing cabinet.
Make sure the headphones are working properly before each session begins.
Do not tell participants which condition they have been assigned to, because that could influence their responses.
After the final task, thank the participant, explain the purpose of the experiment, and give them the payment voucher.

context: You have a part-time job at the campus fitness center. Listen to the facility manager and repeat what he says.
visual: A modern gym with treadmills by the windows, weight machines and a reception counter with towels.
sentences: Please show your student card.
Towels are available at the front desk.
The swimming pool is closed for cleaning on Mondays.
Members must wipe down the machines after they use them.
Beginners can book a free session with a personal trainer each semester.
The yoga and spinning classes fill up quickly, so students should reserve a place online.
If anyone gets injured while exercising, call the first aid officer and fill out an incident report before your shift ends.
